The IRGC Aerospace Force has released footage showing the launch of Qiam-1 and Fattah-1 medium-range ballistic missiles, along with Shahed-136, Shahed-238, and Shahed-107 loitering munitions targeting U.S. military installations across the region.

New Russian military vehicles that recently arrived in the Sahel aboard a Russian cargo ship docking in Lomé, Togo, have been observed moving toward Mali to reinforce the Africa Corps.
Among the vehicles identified are several Tigr-M GAZ-233114 multipurpose armored vehicles, MAZ-6317 and Ural-4320 trucks, as well as one BTR-82A armored personnel carrier and one BMP-3 infantry fighting vehicle.

Prototypes of the French Thundart Multiple Launch Rocket System (MLRS) will undergo testing in Ukraine.
The system is being developed by MBDA and Safran to replace the aging M270 LRU (Lance-Roquettes Unitaire), the French variant of the American M270.
The Thundart's rockets are compatible with the M270 LRU, although their full specifications have not yet been disclosed. The only confirmed detail is a range of 150 km, with plans to increase it to 500 km in the future.
Safran is expected to integrate the same guidance system used in the AASM Hammer family of precision-guided air-to-ground bombs into the rocket.
The launcher is mounted on a Scania 8×8 truck chassis equipped with a rotating launcher mount.

According to the IRGC, its strikes on the King Faisal and Prince Hassan Air Bases destroyed multiple U.S. drones and caused significant damage to military infrastructure.
The IRGC claims it struck an F-15 preparation hangar, destroyed a drone preparation hangar containing eight brand-new MQ-9A unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAVs) that were still in their packaging and had not yet been assembled for service, and heavily damaged two additional drones positioned outside the hangar.
The IRGC also says it hit a helicopter maintenance hangar, causing major damage to two heavy U.S. helicopters, and struck accommodation facilities, killing and injuring several personnel.
